title: SparseTransX: Efficient Training of Translation-Based Knowledge Graph Embeddings Using Sparse Matrix Operations
problem: Training translational knowledge graph embedding (KGE) models (TransE, TransR, TransH, TorusE) is bottlenecked by fine-grained scatter/gather operations during gradient computation (up to 40% of CPU training time), causing irregular memory access patterns, high backpropagation overhead, and large intermediate memory allocations.
motivation: KG training triplets are inherently sparse (each triplet touches only 2-3 entity/relation embeddings out of thousands), yet existing frameworks (TorchKGE, DGL-KE, PyG) use dense PyTorch embedding lookup and fine-grained scatter operations. Sparse matrix operations (SpMM) are highly optimized in GNN libraries but have never been applied to KGE training. Replacing scatter-gather with SpMM unifies multiple embedding operations into a single matrix multiply, enabling cache blocking, SIMD vectorization, WARP-level GPU primitives, and loop unrolling.
method: SparseTransX reformulates translational KGE training by constructing a sparse incidence matrix A from training triplets: each row represents one triplet, with +1 in the head entity column and -1 in the tail entity column (for ht expression) or additionally +1 in the relation column offset by entity count (for hrt expression). Multiplying A (sparse, M x (N+R)) by the embedding matrix E (dense, (N+R) x d) directly computes batched (head - tail) or (head + relation - tail) expressions via a single SpMM call. Both forward and backward pass benefit: backward reduces to SpMM on the transpose A^T. Four models implemented: TransE (hrt computation, L2 norm), TransR (ht computation + per-relation projection matrix Mr applied separately), TransH (two ht computations with hyperplane projections), TorusE (hrt with torus distance). Framework uses iSpLib (CSR format, SIMD vectorized, auto-tuned) for CPU and DGL g-SpMM (COO format) for GPU. PyTorch DDP/FSDP wrappers support distributed training.
key_novelty: First application of SpMM to replace scatter-gather in translational KGE training; sparse incidence matrix formulation that unifies head-tail-relation embedding extraction into a single matrix multiplication enabling high-performance sparse library acceleration.
contributions: Sparse incidence matrix formulation for ht (head-tail) and hrt (head+relation-tail) expressions via SpMM
Sparse formulations for TransE, TransR, TransH, TorusE (and extensibility analysis for DistMult, ComplEx, RotatE)
SparseTransX library: iSpLib (CPU, CSR, SIMD+loop-unrolling+cache-blocking) and DGL g-SpMM (GPU, COO, WARP-level)
11x GPU memory efficiency improvement for TransH over TorchKGE
Streaming embedding support via PyTorch memory-mapped tensors for embeddings too large for CPU memory

metrics.cpu_speedup_transe: up to 5.3x speedup on CPU vs TorchKGE (across 7 datasets including BioKG 4.8M triplets)
metrics.gpu_speedup_transe: up to 4.2x speedup on GPU vs TorchKGE
metrics.gpu_memory_transh: 0.28 GB vs 3.1 GB (TorchKGE) for TransH (11x reduction)

limitations: TorusE speedup is lower than TransE because torus L2 dissimilarity function (not embedding gradient) dominates compute
TransH shows moderate speedup because SpMM accounts for smaller fraction of total training time due to large computational graph
TransR backward is slower than DGL-KE (which uses custom gradient via DGL graph API) on CPU in some configs
Distributed training results shown only as preliminary (Appendix F); not the primary evaluation focus
COO format for GPU requires format conversion overhead for some workloads
